speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you tell me how long you've had these symptoms and if they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis.

(Note: While the father's history of psoriasis and the cold-weather exacerbation might suggest a genetic component or inverse psoriasis, the clinical picture of a 3-month-old with a red, scaly rash on the scalp and forehead is most characteristic of seborrheic dermatitis ("cradle cap"), which commonly appears in this age group and can be worsened by dry weather. I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the age and distribution of the rash, but I will confirm if there is any family history of atopic dermatitis or if there are signs of secondary infection like honey-colored crusts.)
